description: Six stylized surface-ocean environment categories used to sample baseline conditions. These are explicitly NOT claimed to reproduce any specific real-world location.
sampling_note: temperature_c and salinity_psu are sampled uniformly within each archetype's range; initial_total_alkalinity_umol_kg (ta0) is then calculated from a published total alkalinity-salinity relationship plus bounded noise, so alkalinity and salinity covary realistically rather than being sampled independently.

archetypes.name: Polar / subpolar
archetypes.notes: Low aragonite saturation state, high Revelle factor (low buffering capacity)

archetypes.name: Subtropical gyre
archetypes.notes: High alkalinity, high aragonite saturation state

archetypes.name: Tropical
archetypes.notes: Highest aragonite saturation state of the six archetypes

archetypes.name: Coastal, lower salinity
archetypes.notes: Alkalinity from total alkalinity-salinity relation with larger noise term to reflect greater natural variability

archetypes.name: High-salinity marginal sea
archetypes.notes: Mediterranean-like conditions; not claimed to represent the Mediterranean Sea specifically

atmospheric_co2_ppm.note: Fixed in the core dataset (approx. mid-2020s level, NOAA GML); varied in sensitivity runs

baseline_disequilibrium_uatm.note: Represents natural seasonal/biological air-sea CO2 disequilibrium; pco2_0 = atmospheric_co2_ppm + disequilibrium

equilibration_fraction_f.note: Fraction of potential CO2 uptake realized before a treated water parcel may be subducted or mixed away; uncertain parameter varied in Monte Carlo analysis
